messages:
Prashant: Quick Q — planning to start deprecating the implicit/unpinned default-model behavior next month. Thinking 4-week public deprec + 4-week enforcement window. Two asks: (1) can we agree on the client header shape we expect for model/version pinning, and (2) what is the minimal server fallback behavior we guarantee? cc @Sara @Mike

Sara: +1 on announcing asap. For Private customers we need at least a 2-month notice in the console + a migration CLI. Are we sure 4 weeks is enough for hosted users? :thinking:

Mike: I think 4-week deprec + 4-week enforce is OK for public API if we provide an automatic compatibility fallback for older clients. Header proposal: `Accept-Model-Version: <model_name>@<semver|tag>` or `X-Model-Pin: <model>:<version>` — prefer the Accept-* style to align with content negotiation.

Olga: Agree with header. SDKs need a minor bump with clear docs and a deprecation warning at client init. Also add a lint rule in the SDK to detect calls without a pin and log a warning.

Prashant: Good. For server fallback: if header missing, we do - 1) try tenant-pin (org-level) if present, - 2) if not, route to `latest-stable` for N weeks, then reject with 409 + guidance after enforcement window. We should emit telemetry: `model_pin_received`, `model_fallback_used`, `model_reject_after_deprec`.

Luis: Suggestion: carve out a narrow compatibility gate for customers that explicitly opt into `auto-upgrade: true` header. That way some teams can stay on latest without needing code changes. 

Mike: Nice idea. Maybe `Accept-Model-Version: latest; auto-upgrade=1` or `X-Model-Flags: auto-upgrade`. Keep it simple. Also need to document exact error shape for rejection so client SDK can show actionable UI text. Example error: `{code: 409, message: "model pin required after 2026-04-15", details: {help_url}}`

Prashant: Draft server pseudocode for the routing logic — open to feedback:

```
# pseudo
if header Accept-Model-Version:
  target = resolve(header)
elif org_pin:
  target = org_pin
elif within_deprecation_window:
  target = latest_stable
else:
  return 409, {
    "message": "model pin required after <enforce-date>",
    "help_url": "https://docs.redwood.ai/deprecations/model-pinning"
  }
```

Sara: That looks good. One more operational ask: can the console show a per-route pin warning and a bulk-migrate helper that adds a header override for server-side proxies? Product/Docs need this before we announce.

Prashant: Yep — plan: (A) internal announce + docs draft next week, (B) SDK warnings + lint in 2 weeks, (C) public deprec notice 4 weeks before enforce-date, (D) enforcement. For Private/on-prem customers: extend the enforcement by +8 weeks and run a specific migration assist.

Mike: Canary plan — start with 5% of requests on hosted hitting the enforce path (i.e., observe rejections), then 25%, then full. Add a feature flag `enforce_model_pin` per region. deploy-bot: can you queue canary? :pray:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: feature flag `enforce_model_pin` -> region=us-west-2, pct=5, owner=Prashant

Olga: I'll start the SDK PR today to add the warning. Will include upgrade guide and sample header usage in the README.

Luis: I'll add telemetry metrics to the routing service: counts for header present, org_pin used, fallback used, rejects, and client-sdk warning hits. We'll keep an alert if rejects > 0.5% during initial rollout.

Prashant: Action items: - Prashant: draft public docs + deprec notice by EOW - Olga: SDK PR + lint rule by next Tue - Luis: telemetry + alert by next Tue - Mike: coordinate canary windows with infra - Sara: product copy + console pin UX scope. If no objections, I'll publish the internal RFC today. :+1:

Sara: No objections. Please include a short FAQ in the RFC for Private customers (migration options, CLI steps).

Mike: Fine by me. One last ask — confirm exact header examples in docs (both Accept-Model-Version and X-Model-Pin) and say which is preferred. Recommend Accept-Model-Version as canonical.

Prashant: Will do. I'll include both examples and mark `Accept-Model-Version` as preferred. Thanks all.
